commits.message: fix(deploy): state what the multiplexer guarantees on a cross-slot race, against v1.1.0 (rich-workflows-ui0d)
fix(deploy): one concurrency group per docs slot, so a PR run cannot cancel a pending master deploy (rich-workflows-ui0d)

effects: promote the effect catalogue to src/ with a docs page (rich-effects-fxiy.br2) (#338)

* effects: promote the effect catalogue to src/ with a docs page (rich-effects-fxiy.br2)

Shimmer, pulse, sparkle, wheel, fade-in and dissolve-out move from the
effects-feel demo into src/renderables/effects.ts, exported from the main
barrel with the signed-off curves (EFFECT_CURVES), lights (EFFECT_LIGHTS)
and SHIMMER_WIDTH. Their noise moves to src/core/noise.ts, unexported.

fadeIn and dissolveOut now return a Transition: the effect, and done(t).

The demo draws from the library and its own curve file is gone; its flag
defaults derive from EFFECT_CURVES. The effects playground still cuts each
program from the source it plays, now src/renderables/effects.ts plus the
noise it reaches, since the live library admits only public entry points.

Verified: the demo's output at fixed t (1632 frames: every effect, both
subjects, Mocha and Latte, truecolor/256/16, two magnitudes, two transition
starts) is byte-identical before and after the switch.

* effects: review fixes — shape params dropped, curves checked when built, shares refuses an unpaired colour (rich-effects-fxiy.br2)

fadeIn/dissolveOut no longer take a shape: no caller passed one, and an
own above 1 made done() lie. Each builds its phase once, so a curve with
no duration throws as it is made; transition output unchanged (old vs new
compared over 216k cell-frames, 0 differ). The playground cuts each
declaration from its own doc comment, so noise.ts's file header no longer
lands in programs. Docs example draws on Mocha's ground; stale curves.ts
pointers fixed.

* effects: a curve's swing is checked when its effect is made; an overshooting ease saturates (rich-effects-fxiy.br2)

requireCurve, at each effect's construction, refuses a seconds that is not
positive and a swing outside [0, 1]. A field or visibility outside [0, 1] —
what a CSS cubic-bezier with overshoot yields — is held to it where strength
is consumed (onColors, veiled), so dissolveOut's own clamp goes. In-range
values are untouched.
